jordan_acme: Hey team — we started seeing a bunch of 429s on our streaming _chat-completions_ traffic around 09:14 UTC. Only affects streaming endpoints, non-streaming calls are fine. No deploys on our side. Any immediate ideas?

sam_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the top of a response body or the client error? Also how many concurrent streams and tokens/sec roughly?

jordan_acme: Error payload: `HTTP/2 429` with body `{"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded"}}`. We generally run 30 long-lived streams per pod, ~250 requests/min total across 6 pods. Streams are mostly keepalive + periodic user messages.

maya_sre: Quick hypothesis: TPM (tokens/min) or RPM (requests/min) bursts when user messages spike may be tripping the global policy. Streaming sessions still count when you send a trailing message. Are you multiplexing multiple streams over one HTTP/2 connection?

jordan_acme: Yes — we use HTTP/2 with 8 concurrent streams per connection (nghttp2 via gRPC-ish client). Usually keeps connections open.

eli_runtime: Reproduced similar pattern in the past: multiplexing + keepalive can cause many logical streams to appear at the same time on the server side when clients flush multiple messages quickly, which can look like a burst. Also if your client reuses one connection across many instances, token accounting can be bunched by the edge.

sam_support: Can you share a short capture of request timestamps (just the last 3 minutes)? Even a summarized histogram of requests/sec or tokens/sec would help. In the meantime, try this mitigation: set client max concurrent streams to 2 and add jittered backoff on 429s.

jordan_acme: Attaching a mini-snippet of their client logs (sanitized):
```
[09:12:34] send stream msg userId=42 size=340 tokens=18
[09:12:34] send stream msg userId=87 size=120 tokens=6
[09:12:34] keepalive ping
[09:12:35] send stream msg userId=42 size=512 tokens=25
[09:12:36] recv 429 for stream id=5
```

maya_sre: That stampy pattern — lots of messages in the same second — will show up as a tiny burst and can exceed the per-minute rolling bucket if your traffic is bucketed oddly. Two practical items: 1) stagger client writes across a small random window (50–200ms) and 2) add exponential backoff with jitter for 429s instead of immediate retry loops.

eli_runtime: On our side I checked the rate-limiter logs for your org id — saw short 20–40s windows where the token-bucket headroom went negative, then recovered. Looks like a low-burst cap kicking in (our soft-burst policy). I'm opening an internal ticket to review the burst threshold for your org.

sam_support: For immediate relief we can temporarily raise your burst allowance for the next 2 hours while you patch the client. Would you like us to apply that? Also please confirm the org id and example request ids.

jordan_acme: Yes please raise it for 2 hours. Org id ACME-1337. Example request-id: req_2026_3632109909. We'll roll the client change in the next deploy (stagger + reduce streams to 3 per connection).

maya_sre: Got it — I'll apply a short burst increase and add an annotation so engineering knows it's elevated. Eli, assigning to you to check whether edge multiplexing aggregation could be smearing per-connection metrics.

eli_runtime: Assigning ENG-RUNTIME ticket INF-8243. Action items: (1) audit per-connection aggregation codepath, (2) add a debug flag to emit per-stream accounting for customer requests for short windows, (3) confirm whether keepalive-only streams are being considered active for bucket window.

sam_support: deploy-bot: applied temporary burst increase for ACME-1337 for 120m.

deploy-bot: [automated] Temporary ratecap override applied: org=ACME-1337 duration=120m ticket=INF-8243.

jordan_acme: Thanks all — I’ll test after we push the client limiter and report back in ~40m. Appreciate the quick turn. :thumbsup:

maya_sre: Follow-up: if you still see 429s after the client patch, capture a short pcap or sequence of request timestamps and send to us (TLP: support only). We can also provision a short Dedicated slot if you need guaranteed capacity while you scale.

eli_runtime: Will update INF-8243 with any kernel/aggregation findings. Keeping monitoring on your org bucket; ping here if it recurs.
